regime: Oil-transport escalation remains the immediate inflation shock, but demand destruction/rerouting is now visible enough to cap a simplistic one-way oil thesis. Restrictive real/nominal yields and widening weak-end credit stress are a co-dominant valuation regime. AI physical capex remains expansionary and increasingly differentiated by funded backlog and cash conversion.

keyReadings.label: Hormuz commodity traffic
keyReadings.value: ~10 ships/day latest 10-day average; lowest since May

keyReadings.label: CCC-and-lower spread
keyReadings.note: Reported spread statistic, not an inferred live ICE index tick; up from 8.08pp a year earlier.

keyReadings.label: Fed September hike probability
keyReadings.value: ~50% current reporting range ahead of CPI

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: US resilient; Asian energy demand destruction visible
channels.interpretation: US jobs/services remain expansionary, but China's seaborne crude imports show material conflict-driven demand/routing adaptation.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.regime: Hike risk remains meaningful ahead of CPI
channels.interpretation: Oil inflation and resilient activity keep clean policy relief unlikely; current reporting places September hike odds around even-money rather than a one-way bet.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.regime: Restrictive real/nominal yields plus global rate pressure
channels.interpretation: 2Y ~4.37%, 10Y ~4.79%, 30Y ~5.25% and real 10Y ~2.45% keep duration expensive; BOJ tightening risk adds global pressure.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.interpretation: Quality borrowers retain access, but capital competition and high base rates are increasingly punitive for marginal issuers.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: Reported CCC-and-lower spreads around 10.53pp and rising default actions make weak balance sheets a first-class risk filter.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.interpretation: Employment supports incomes, but high gasoline/diesel and financing costs continue to squeeze discretionary purchasing power.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: Long yields remain hostile to mortgage affordability; no fresh evidence reverses this.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.interpretation: Foxconn record August revenue and stronger Q3 AI outlook reinforce ISM/equipment evidence that physical AI demand is real. Funding quality remains the gate.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.interpretation: Oil/product/shipping stress sits on top of ISM Prices >70 and constrained electrical/electronic inputs.

channels.label: Labour
channels.interpretation: NFP +162k and unemployment 4.1% remain stronger than the weak ISM Services Employment signal alone.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.interpretation: Oil/geopolitical risk and restrictive yields offset resilient AI earnings evidence; Monday US cash session has not occurred at this cut.

channels.label: Crude
channels.regime: Severe transport constraint with demand offset
channels.interpretation: Direct tanker attacks and low Hormuz traffic keep scarcity acute, but China import compression proves high prices/disruption are destroying or rerouting demand.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: Refined-product scarcity remains more economically important than flat crude alone; China fuel exports and rerouting are the offset to monitor.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.interpretation: Gulf route risk increases the strategic value of US/Atlantic LNG, though no fresh US domestic gas shortage was verified.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.interpretation: Fiscal/geopolitical hedge remains valid, but real yields near 2.45% and USD/Fed risk argue against chasing.

channels.label: Copper / Industrial Metals
channels.interpretation: Grid demand remains strong but elevated/distorted visible inventories prevent treating copper as a clean immediate shortage.
